keyFacts: Posterization reduces each color channel to a fixed number of evenly spaced steps.
With 4 levels per channel, the image uses at most 4 × 4 × 4 = 64 distinct colors.
Lower level counts create flat, graphic, poster-like regions of color.
Higher level counts keep the photo realistic with only a slight stylized feel.
The output keeps the original pixel dimensions.

limitations: Posterization is a stylistic effect — it intentionally discards smooth gradients.
Very low level counts can merge faces into unrecognizable blobs.
The effect applies to the whole image; selective-area posterization is not included.
Animated GIFs are processed as a single still frame.

posterize-effect.workedExample:
A channel value of 100 with 3 levels:
step = 255 / (3 − 1) = 127.5
level = round(100 / 255 × 2) = round(0.784) = 1
output = round(1 × 127.5) = 128
So every channel can only be 0, 128, or 255, and the whole image uses at most 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 distinct colors.
